findings.finding: Fault-side identity cannot be recovered from a parcel centroid.
findings.evidence: An independent flat–ramp–flat example keeps all true material on the hanging-wall side while its exact centroid falls on the other side. Reclassifying a translated rectangle around that centroid incorrectly stops material on a later slip.
findings.qualification: This proves a limitation of the replacement geometry. It does not by itself prove that every stored-coordinate versus offset-coordinate discrepancy in a coupled run is a wrong-side transport error.

findings.finding: Storage placement affects later accommodation and deposition.
findings.evidence: In the A diagnostic, a 36.016 m storage-surface difference develops near the right boundary before the troublesome bed is deposited; the first transported rock markers differ by about 0.000091 m. The B diagnostic likewise links a storage-floor jump to a later deposit-thickness discrepancy.
findings.qualification: The first rock marker is not an authoritative surface at the storage column x when it has a horizontal offset. A surface-only replacement is therefore insufficient.

findings.finding: The worst fine-grid C travel discrepancy is generated by coupled operations.
findings.evidence: At x=3600 m, the current 20–10 m difference ends at −5.585599 ms. Step 19 thrust slip contributes −4.135191 ms to the difference, followed by additional compaction amplification.
findings.qualification: The recorded material flow offsets agree with an independent affine flow calculation. Closing the sediment budget and computing those offsets correctly does not ensure a consistent material geometry through later processes.

findings.finding: Compaction needs a common material-and-fault mapping.
findings.evidence: A two-bed analytical fixture begins with coherent, nonoverlapping physical beds but different storage offsets. Current compaction moves a point from 1 m above a fault to 4.5 m below it while the fault stays fixed.
findings.qualification: Persistent fault-side labels alone would not reconcile this mapping inconsistency or recover a lost material footprint.

guard_review.review: Read-only review; no source changes or simulation/test reruns.
guard_review.decision: No blocking defect. Valid narrow same-thrust mobility, final centroid, and conservation regression guard; insufficient as a general geology or convergence acceptance test.
what_the_guard_proves: The tagged sediment remains included in retained second-slip transport after first slipping around the same fault upper bend, at40/20/10m.
The test requires complete tagged grain inclusion, unchanged constituent grain/composition/memories, input purity, and closed budgets for both slips.
After the second slip, the tagged material has independently expected total height2m and physical means x=−1400+h,z=499m. An identity-transfer implementation no longer satisfies these assertions.
limits: Passing does not establish correct baseline geology or validate its storage-coordinate classifier in general. That classifier can pass this particular fixture while failing other physical-coordinate identities.

The initial bed bottom lies exactly on the lower-flat fault. Positive side distance holds for its interior, almost everywhere; the zero-measure boundary does not invalidate the material-volume expectation.

The new assertion closes the previous untested-motion limitation. It constrains final moments and volume, not the full distribution or intermediate deformed shape; the separate analytical bend proof remains relevant.
The test does not cover differential-offset compaction, other faults, newly deposited or incoming material, finite-width side clipping, or memory/runtime behavior.
The existing assessment correctly records that its subsequent mean-flow diagnostic is exact in the symmetric fixture. It does not falsely claim a repeated-centroid-flow defect.
minimum_next_representation_acceptance: Pass this strengthened mobility/final-motion guard and the separate independent intermediate-bend geometry proof, with conservation and source purity. Correct means alone must not authorize reclassification of lost support.

Define the authoritative physical-support/topology contract. Preserve side information under same-fault flow through a coherent footprint or equivalent metadata; never infer true side solely from a centroid replacement rectangle.

Resolve or explicitly bound the proven differential-offset compaction counterexample. A material point and its fault must follow a compatible common physical map if side invariance is claimed; immutable labels alone do not repair this.

Specify and test membership/support propagation through exact slicing, raster/rebuild, coalescing, compaction, subsidence, collapse, new deposition, erosion, incoming continuation, and later faults. Opposite memberships must not merge; basement metadata cannot silently disappear.

Retain every positive distinct material component, grains/composition and irreversible history; maintain exact support/capacity consistency and explicit boundary ledgers. No silent trimming or history averaging to obtain feasibility.
Demonstrate bounded part count, successful full-depth runs, and memory/runtime within the established environment; avoid recurring footprint or fragment explosion.

Run the unchanged full test suite and the frozen 12-case, 36-run 40/20/10 m synthetic comparison, with all budgets, complete paired coverage, outliers and all metrics disclosed. Keep holdout and observational arrays untouched.

Tie release claims to demonstrated results. Mixed grid agreement can support a narrowly described correctness repair, but cannot establish that the requested travel-time/thickness regressions are fixed; unresolved regressions and unvalidated design work must remain explicit.

closed_form_assertion_review.derivation: Write source point x=−1720+y with y in[−h/2,h/2],z=700−δ with δ in[0,2]. Let c=√2−1. The offset ramp length is200√2; its two intersections shift left bycδ. After total slip120+200√2+h, arc position beyond the upper bend is h+y+cδ≥h/2>0. Thus every true point is on the upper flat, with final x=−1400+h+y,z=500−δ. Uniform rectangle means are−1400+h and499, and height remains2. No production helper is used to derive these expectations.
closed_form_assertion_review.coverage_limit: The final mean and total-height assertions do not reconstruct the whole intermediate deformed support or prove every intermediate point is represented correctly.
